passages.text:
🏦 RBI MPC • June 3–5, 2026
RBI Holds Repo Rate at 5.25% — Neutral Stance Retained Amid West Asia Conflict, Fuel Inflation, and Monsoon Risks
The Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to pause — citing elevated energy prices, supply-chain disruptions, and a deficient monsoon forecast — while raising the FY27 inflation projection to 5.1% and keeping GDP growth pegged at 6.6%.
5.25%● UnchangedRepo Rate
Neutral● RetainedMPC Stance
6.6%● FY27 ForecastReal GDP Growth
5.1%▲ RaisedCPI Inflation FY27
The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, concluded its second meeting of FY 2026-27 on June 5, 2026 — and in a widely anticipated but carefully worded decision, chose to hold the policy repo rate steady at 5.25% and retain its 'neutral' monetary policy stance. The decision was taken by a unanimous 6-0 vote. The pause comes after cumulative rate cuts of 100 basis points since the rate-cutting cycle began in February 2025 — and reflects the MPC's assessment that growing uncertainty from the prolonged West Asia conflict, elevated energy prices, and an uncertain monsoon calls for watchful caution rather than further easing.

The RBI has cumulatively cut the repo rate by 100 bps (1 percentage point) in this easing cycle — from 6.50% to 5.25%. The June 2026 pause is the first after a full year of intermittent easing, signalling that the MPC is now in a data-dependent watchful mode rather than an easing mode.
⚖️ Section 3 — What Does 'Neutral' Stance Mean?
The MPC has retained its 'neutral' monetary policy stance. Understanding what this means — and why it matters — is crucial for interpreting the RBI's forward guidance.
🔴 'Accommodative' Stance (Until Jun 2025)
Signalled MPC's bias towards further rate cuts. Each decision leant toward easing monetary conditions to support growth. Rate hikes were off the table.
🟡 'Neutral' Stance (Since Jun 2025)
No pre-committed direction. The MPC can move rates either up or down — or hold. The next step depends entirely on incoming inflation, growth, and external data. Both tightening and easing remain live options.

passages.title: RBI MPC Meeting Highlights: Repo Rate Unchanged at 5.25%, Retains Neutral Stance
passages.text:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent and retained its neutral stance at its August monetary policy review. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) also raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7 percent from 6.6 percent and lowered its CPI inflation projection to 5 percent from 5.1 percent.
Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the MPC chose to hold rates because it wanted "greater clarity" on the inflation outlook before taking any policy action. While headline inflation has moved above the 4 percent target, he said the increase was largely driven by food and fuel prices, with "little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far".
The RBI expects headline inflation to peak in the October-December quarter before easing. It also flagged renewed tensions in West Asia, volatile crude oil prices, an uneven southwest monsoon amid El Niño conditions and global trade uncertainty as key risks to growth and inflation.
At the post-policy press conference, Malhotra said the RBI was "neither dovish nor hawkish" and would continue to be guided by headline inflation, with future policy decisions depending on how growth and inflation evolve.

passages.title: RBI MPC Meeting Highlights: Repo Rate Unchanged at 5.25%, Retains Neutral Stance
passages.text:
Dalcore: Stability in the interest rate environment helps sustain buyer confidence
Sidharth Chowdhry, managing director, Dalcore, says, “The RBI’s decision to maintain the repo rate provides much-needed policy continuity for both developers and homebuyers. Stability in the interest rate environment helps sustain buyer confidence, particularly in the premium and luxury housing segment where purchase decisions are driven by long-term wealth creation and lifestyle aspirations rather than short-term market fluctuations. A predictable monetary environment further strengthens this momentum, enabling the sector to maintain healthy growth while supporting long-term investment confidence.”
Federal Bank: RBI remains in wait-and-watch mode
“The policy with a neutral stance is clearly guiding a wait-and-watch mode on future rate direction, based on how the growth-inflation dynamics play out in the coming periods,” said Lakshmanan V, group president and head of treasury at Federal Bank.
He said the key risks to watch would be the southwest monsoon, El Niño, geopolitical developments and global trade policy.
Muthoot Finance: Stable rates improve visibility on funding costs

passages.text:
He said the key risks to watch would be the southwest monsoon, El Niño, geopolitical developments and global trade policy.
Muthoot Finance: Stable rates improve visibility on funding costs
“The RBI’s decision to maintain the repo rate at 5.25 percent while retaining a neutral stance reflects a prudent and forward-looking assessment of the evolving macroeconomic environment,” said George Alexander Muthoot, managing director of Muthoot Finance.
He added that with the policy rate remaining steady, NBFCs have greater visibility on funding costs and credit planning, creating a conducive environment for sustained disbursements. “Stability at this stage of the rate cycle is positive for both lenders and borrowers, as it supports business confidence, encourages productive credit demand and enables timely access to formal finance for households, entrepreneurs and MSMEs.”
